criteria_results.title: Identifies A-Number transposition error (845 vs. 854)
criteria_results.reasoning: Finding A-1 identifies I-797C A-217-854-903 vs submission A-217-845-903, digits transposed.

criteria_results.title: Categorizes A-Number transposition as Critical severity
criteria_results.reasoning: A-1 is rated CRITICAL.

criteria_results.title: Explains A-Number error impact on I-485 case linkage
criteria_results.reasoning: A-1 explains the wrong A-Number may misassociate the petition and cause problems when the I-140 is relied on for the I-485.

criteria_results.title: Recommends corrective action for A-Number error (e-Request/service request)
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends a typographical-error correction via the USCIS e-Request portal or Contact Center plus a written request to TSC.

criteria_results.title: Identifies missing middle name 'Priya' on receipt notice
criteria_results.reasoning: A-2 identifies receipt shows 'Ananya Mehta' vs 'Ananya Priya Mehta' in cover letter.

criteria_results.title: Categorizes missing middle name as Moderate (not Critical) severity
criteria_results.reasoning: The middle-name omission is rated HIGH on a four-tier scale where MEDIUM is the mid level, so it is not Moderate or Low as required.

criteria_results.title: Notes G-28 also omits middle name, creating ambiguity
criteria_results.reasoning: Notes G-28 leaves middle name blank and that the omission may have originated there or on the I-140, so it is unclear whether USCIS caused it.

criteria_results.title: Identifies that I-797C shows only $715 fee, not total $3,520
criteria_results.reasoning: A-5 notes the I-797C acknowledges only $715 while one $3,520 check covered $715 + $2,805.

criteria_results.title: Correctly explains premium processing fee absence is standard practice
criteria_results.reasoning: The report rates the missing I-907 fee on the receipt as Critical and lists the fee line as a discrepancy. It never says this is standard practice and not an error.

criteria_results.title: Identifies delivery date vs. receipt date gap (March 15 vs. March 17)
criteria_results.reasoning: A-4 identifies FedEx delivery on Saturday March 15 vs receipt date Monday March 17.

criteria_results.title: Notes cover letter states filing date as March 15 vs. receipt date March 17
criteria_results.reasoning: C-4 and the comparison table note the cover letter's 'Date of Filing: March 15, 2025' vs the March 17 receipt date.

criteria_results.title: Explains weekend lockbox processing as reason for date gap
criteria_results.reasoning: It mentions next-business-day dating of weekend deliveries only in passing and argues the date should be corrected to March 15. It does not conclude March 17 is correct.

criteria_results.title: Identifies petitioner name styling difference on receipt
criteria_results.reasoning: A-3 identifies 'Helion Biosciences Inc' vs 'Helion BioSciences, Inc.' with the capitalization and punctuation differences.

criteria_results.title: Assesses petitioner name styling as Low severity
criteria_results.reasoning: A-3 rated LOW.

criteria_results.title: Recommends matching I-485 petitioner name to receipt notice version
criteria_results.reasoning: No guidance on which petitioner name version to use on the I-485; it only suggests confirming the legal name and possibly requesting a correction.

criteria_results.title: Identifies internal fee inconsistency: checklist says $700 vs. cover letter $715
criteria_results.reasoning: B-2 identifies the checklist's $700/$3,505 vs the cover letter's $715/$3,520.

criteria_results.title: Explains checklist used outdated pre-April 2024 fee ($700)
criteria_results.reasoning: B-2 explains $700 is the fee before April 1, 2024 and that $715 in the cover letter is correct.

criteria_results.title: Recommends updating checklist template to use current fee
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends correcting the Fee Summary and updating the firm's fee template, with attorney sign-off against the current fee schedule.

criteria_results.title: Flags absence of separate I-907 receipt notice
criteria_results.reasoning: A-5 flags that no separate I-907 premium processing receipt is in the file.

criteria_results.title: Categorizes missing I-907 receipt as Critical or High given timeline
criteria_results.reasoning: A-5 rated CRITICAL.

criteria_results.title: Recommends verifying I-907 receipt status urgently
criteria_results.reasoning: Recommends checking mail logs and the USCIS account for an I-907 receipt immediately and, if none, contacting USCIS right away.

criteria_results.title: Report contains recommended action items tied to April 30 deadline
criteria_results.reasoning: There is an action plan, but it never mentions the April 30, 2025 I-485 deadline.

criteria_results.title: Correctly states the USCIS receipt number as SRC-25-901-12478
criteria_results.reasoning: Receipt number SRC-25-901-12478 is stated accurately.

criteria_results.title: Explains impact of missing I-907 receipt on processing timeline
criteria_results.reasoning: It does not tie the missing I-907 receipt to standard processing times or to the April 30 I-485 deadline.

criteria_results.title: Identifies that the check was written for $3,520 confirming correct fees paid
criteria_results.reasoning: It notes the $3,520 check but concludes the payment was $600 short (Asylum Program Fee), so it does not confirm the correct fees were paid.

criteria_results.title: Addresses potential I-485 impact for middle name omission
criteria_results.reasoning: A-2 says the name should match the passport and later I-485 records, and that the variance raises misidentification and RFE risk at the I-485 stage.
